# Case Numbers

**Status:** v3.10 — 2026-11-20; intro: numbers generated by CIS are created outside DRISTI, which records and shows each once CIS has generated it; how DRISTI receives them is in [`cis-integration.md`](cis-integration.md). v3.9 — 2026-11-20; each state's format table has a *Generated by* column (DRISTI or CIS). v3.8 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-17`: the CRM number never becomes the case's active number. v3.7 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-14`: in Punjab & Haryana, DRISTI generates the filing number when the draft case is created, and it identifies the case from then on; new `CNO-14a`: the CNR comes from CIS when the case is submitted (`Q-3` answered). v3.6 — 2026-11-20; new `CNO-17`: in Punjab & Haryana a case can get a CRM number from CIS; nothing triggers it in this version. New §4 Enhancements (`ENH-01`): a specific type of order item will trigger it. Open questions are now §5. v3.5 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-14`: the filing number and CNR come when the case is submitted; the filing number's format is left to the developers — simple and easy for people to read and understand. `Q-3` reworded to match. v3.4 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-04`: a case dismissed before cognizance gets no case number; no longer says that not taking cognizance means the matter is disposed of. v3.3 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-03`: says the type chosen for the filing number is usually not changed at registration. v3.2 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-02`–`CNO-04`: CIS generates the filing, registration and case numbers in the expected formats in the table; how CIS counts them is no longer described, and the Gujarat format table gives the plain pattern. v3.1 — 2026-11-20; `CNO-01`: the draft number's format is left to the developers — simple and easy for people to read and understand (`Q-2` answered). v3 — 2026-11-20; Kerala (§1) and Punjab & Haryana (§3) rewritten as requirements the same way as Gujarat: Kerala `CNO-08`–`CNO-13`, Punjab & Haryana `CNO-14`–`CNO-16`, each with a format table; the active number is always the latest given in every state. Intro no longer explains table columns. New `Q-3`. v2 — 2026-11-20; Gujarat (§2) rewritten as requirements `CNO-01`–`CNO-07` with a format table: DRISTI generates a draft number that identifies the case; the filing number comes at completion of scrutiny and the registration number at registration, each with the type chosen by court staff; the case number (eCC) at cognizance; filing, registration and case numbers and the CNR come from CIS; the active number is always the latest given. New §4 Open questions (`Q-1`, `Q-2`). v1 — 2026-10-19; case numbers only; application, evidence, witness and access-code
numbers removed for now. Kerala: every number generated by DRISTI — filing number at draft,
CMP and CNR at registration, ST at cognizance, LP when the case moves to the long pending
register. Gujarat: filled from the Case Numbering System sheet, plus a DRISTI pre-filing
number. Punjab & Haryana: NACT filing number, CNR and case number from the same sheet.
Earlier drafts: 2026-09-09, 2026-09-15.

**Date:** 2026-11-20

Format, timing and source all differ by state, so each state has its own section. Where a
state registers a case as one of several types, the type is chosen at Scrutiny and Registration —
[`scrutiny-registration.md`](scrutiny-registration.md) `SCR-13`.

Numbers generated by CIS are created in CIS, outside DRISTI. DRISTI records and shows a CIS
number once CIS has generated it. How DRISTI receives it is covered by the CIS integration
([`cis-integration.md`](cis-integration.md)).

---

## 1. Kerala

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `CNO-08` | When a draft case is created, the case gets a filing number. This number identifies the case from then on. |
| `CNO-09` | When the case is registered, it gets a CMP number (Criminal Miscellaneous Petition) and a CNR (Case Number Record). |
| `CNO-10` | When cognizance is taken, the case gets an ST number. |
| `CNO-11` | When the case moves to the long pending register, it gets an LP number (Long Pending). |
| `CNO-12` | DRISTI generates every one of these numbers. |
| `CNO-13` | The case's active number is always the latest number it has been given: the filing number, then the CMP number, then the ST number, then the LP number. |

| Number | Format | Sample | Generated by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Filing number | `[tenantId]-[6-digit sequence]-[year]` | `KL-000049-2025` | DRISTI |
| CMP number | `CMP/[sequence]/[year]` | `CMP/58/2025` | DRISTI |
| CNR | `[courtId][6-digit sequence][year]` — 16 characters | `KLKM520000232025` | DRISTI |
| ST number | `ST/[sequence]/[year]` | `ST/6/2025` | DRISTI |
| LP number | `LP/[sequence]/[year]` | `LP/29/2025` | DRISTI |

---

## 2. Gujarat

Gujarat registers a case as one of three types, each with its own series: **eCC** Criminal
Case, **eCR EN** Criminal Inquiry Case, **eCR MA** Criminal Miscellaneous Application
([`scrutiny-registration.md`](scrutiny-registration.md) `SCR-13`).

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `CNO-01` | When a draft case is created, DRISTI generates a number for it. This number identifies the case from then on. The developers choose its format; it should be simple, and easy for people to read and understand. |
| `CNO-02` | When scrutiny is completed, the case gets a filing number. Scrutiny is completed at Forward for registration or, where the same person scrutinises and registers the case, at Register ([`scrutiny-registration.md`](scrutiny-registration.md) `SCR-11`). The court staff member chooses the type — eCC, eCR EN or eCR MA — and CIS generates the filing number. The expected format is in the table below. |
| `CNO-03` | When the case is registered, it gets a registration number. The court staff member chooses the type again. Usually the type chosen for the filing number (`CNO-02`) is not changed, but it may be changed to either of the other two. CIS generates the registration number. The expected format is in the table below. |
| `CNO-04` | When cognizance is taken, the case gets a case number. Every registered type becomes eCC, and CIS generates the case number. The expected format is in the table below. A case that is dismissed without cognizance being taken gets no case number. |
| `CNO-05` | With the filing number, the case gets a CNR (Case Number Record). The CNR does not change after that — through a change of type, registration, cognizance and disposal. |
| `CNO-06` | The filing number, registration number, case number and CNR all come from CIS. |
| `CNO-07` | The case's active number is always the latest number it has been given: the draft number, then the filing number, then the registration number, then the case number. |

| Number | Type | Format | Sample | Generated by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft number | — | Chosen by the developers (`CNO-01`) | — | DRISTI |
| Filing number | eCC | `eCC/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCC/7/2026` | CIS |
| Filing number | eCR EN | `eCR EN/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCR EN/7/2026` | CIS |
| Filing number | eCR MA | `eCR MA/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCR MA/7/2026` | CIS |
| Registration number | eCC | `eCC/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCC/11/2026` | CIS |
| Registration number | eCR EN | `eCR EN/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCR EN/11/2026` | CIS |
| Registration number | eCR MA | `eCR MA/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCR MA/11/2026` | CIS |
| Case number | eCC | `eCC/[sequence]/[year]` | `eCC/3/2026` | CIS |
| CNR | — | `GJAH` + 2-digit court ID + 6-digit sequence + 4-digit year | `GJAH010001252026` | CIS |

---

## 3. Punjab & Haryana

A §138 case is registered as **NACT** (Negotiable Instruments Act).

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `CNO-14` | When a draft case is created, DRISTI generates its filing number. This number identifies the case from then on. The developers choose its format; it should be simple, and easy for people to read and understand. |
| `CNO-14a` | When the case is submitted, it gets a CNR (Case Number Record) from CIS. |
| `CNO-15` | When the case is registered, it gets a case number, also called the registration number, from CIS. |
| `CNO-16` | The case's active number is always the latest number it has been given: the filing number, then the case number. |
| `CNO-17` | A case can also get a CRM number (Criminal Miscellaneous Registration Number). CIS generates it. It does not become the case's active number. In this version nothing in DRISTI triggers it (`ENH-01`). |

| Number | Format | Sample | Generated by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Filing number | Chosen by the developers (`CNO-14`) | — | DRISTI |
| CNR | Panchkula Special NI Act Court: `HRPK03` + 6-digit sequence + year | `HRPK030096462026` | CIS |
| Case number | `NACT/[sequence]/[year]` | `NACT/566/2026` | CIS |
| CRM number | `CRM-[sequence]-[year]` | `CRM-1953-2025` | CIS |
